newsitem.title: USA: H-P led '96 U.S. Pentium Pro sales - survey.
newsitem.headline: H-P led '96 U.S. Pentium Pro sales - survey.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said its HP Vectra PCs were the best-selling PCs running Intel Corp Pentium Pro chips in the United States in 1996, according to data compiled by Audits and Surveys Worldwide.

The market research firm said HP Vectra PCs were the best-selling Pentium Pro PCs during 1996 in the corporate resale channel, which accounts for 99 percent of Pentium Pro sales within the United States.
The report said Hewlett-Packard held a 44 percent share of the U.S. Pentium Pro market versus Compaq Computer Corp's 39 percent.
Dell Computer Corp held seven percent and Gateway 2000 Inc held three percent, the survey found.
New York-based Audits and Surveys Worldwide is a U.S. sales channel tracking service that measures actual sales from more than 2,000 dealer and retail storefronts.
